scope_statement: Every corpus manifest records governance.provider_transfer as requires_separate_provider_terms_review or blocked. This review is that separate step. It decides, for one named external lane and one named corpus at a time, whether a private copy of clips may be transmitted to that provider for developer benchmarking. It is an engineering record written by the implementing agent, not legal advice, and it does not grant any scientific or product release. Version 1.2.0 extends the same single permitted Azure and SpeechOcean762 pair from the checkpoint 22E4 frozen comparison to the checkpoint 22E4B powered replication, which needs every non held out adult speaker because the recorded no_selection rested on a sample of 8 of 77 development adults and 4 of 25 tuning adults. Nothing else changes: child speakers, held out speakers, Australian Common Voice, every other lane and all owner audio remain excluded exactly as before.
not_legal_advice: This review records the licence text, provider terms and documentation the implementer read, with dates and sources, so the reasoning can be audited or overturned. Adam remains the decision maker for any commercial or legal risk.
principles: a pair that is not listed here is prohibited; absence is never permission
a corpus whose manifest sets provider_transfer to blocked can never be listed as permitted
permission to transmit is not permission to publish results; publication rights are recorded separately in the provider register

transmit the smallest sample that answers the question; where a frozen gate must be passed separately on the development and the threshold tuning partitions, both of those partitions are the smallest sufficient sample and nothing beyond them is permitted
prefer adult speakers when a question can be answered without child speech
no personal or owner audio is covered by this review under any circumstance
a held out speaker is never transmitted, at any checkpoint, for any question
personal_audio_statement: Adam's own recordings in /audio are excluded from every decision in the decisions list below. No corpus decision permits sending owner or user audio to any external provider. Owner audio may leave the machine only through an explicit, separately recorded owner decision naming one exact file by hash, listed under owner_audio_decisions. Absence of such an entry is prohibition.

owner_audio_policy.granting_authority: Adam only, stated explicitly in the working session; never inferred from a general instruction to test or to use the system
owner_audio_policy.scope_rule: each grant covers one named file identified by SHA256, one named lane and one named purpose; it never generalises to other recordings, other lanes or later purposes
owner_audio_policy.user_audio_rule: no grant here may ever cover a recording of anyone other than Adam himself; third party or future user audio needs its own consent design and is outside this review

owner_audio_decisions.granted_by: Adam, stated explicitly in the working session as you can use azure the full system, after being told that the transfer review otherwise excludes his own audio
limitations: one speaker is not a population, so nothing here estimates Australian performance
a performed American accent is not a native American accent, so the American pass is not an American reference
neither pass carries expert human phone labels, so no production is known to be correct or incorrect
this can never become accuracy evidence, a threshold, a selection input, a validation or a gate result
owner_audio_decisions.privacy_note: Azure processes real time pronunciation assessment audio in server memory in australiaeast without retaining it, which is why this lane was the one Adam was asked about.
owner_audio_decisions.purpose: Demonstrate how one external scorer's output moves when the same speaker reads the same eight sentences twice, once in his native Australian accent and once aiming at American, holding speaker, words and room constant. This isolates the variety effect that is otherwise tangled with speaker differences, and specifically tests whether the two control sentences of dialect stable consonants also move.
owner_audio_decisions.scope_note: Covers this one file only, sent to Azure pronunciation assessment only, for this one demonstration. It does not permit sending any other owner recording, does not permit any other lane, and does not create a standing permission. Adam is the only speaker in this recording; no other person's voice is present.

decisions.licence_basis: CC BY 4.0. Section 2(a)(1)(A) grants a worldwide, royalty free, irrevocable licence to reproduce and Share the licensed material in whole or in part. Transmitting a private copy to a processor acting on our behalf is a reproduction. It is not Share, which section 1 defines as providing material to the public, so the section 3(a)(1) attribution conditions, which apply if You Share the licensed material, are not triggered by the transmission itself. Attribution is retained in the corpus manifest regardless and will accompany any published result.
decisions.privacy_basis: The corpus is a public research release. Real time pronunciation assessment audio is not retained or stored by Microsoft, and the resource is deployed in australiaeast. The corpus manifest prohibition on reidentification is unaffected because no speaker identity is transmitted, only a safe clip identifier held locally.
decisions.provider_terms_basis: Microsoft requires the customer to hold the rights to content it inputs, which CC BY 4.0 supplies. Microsoft acts as the customer's third party cloud service processor and does not claim ownership of submitted audio.
decisions.sensitivity_notes: SpeechOcean762 contains both adult and child second language speakers. Child clips are excluded from every transmission under this decision, at checkpoint 22E3 because the schema question did not need them and at checkpoint 22E4 because the frozen gates are adult only, so child speech cannot contribute to a threshold, a gate or a selection and transmitting it would buy nothing. The frozen sample holds only two positive child relations in development and four in tuning, so no child estimate from it could be trusted in any case.

checkpoint_22e3_transmission_plan.justification: Five short adult development clips, each sent twice per locale, is the smallest sample that can both confirm which documented fields actually appear and show whether identical requests return identical responses. Child clips, tuning clips, held out clips and every other corpus are excluded because they are not needed to answer the schema question.

supersedes.note: Versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 stay on disk unchanged as the record of what was decided before each earlier transmission. Both are still validated by the tests so a later edit cannot quietly rewrite that history. Nothing permitted there is withdrawn here, and nothing refused there is granted here.

checkpoint_22e4_transmission_plan.justification: The frozen selection gates must be evaluated separately on the development and the threshold tuning adult partitions, so both are required and neither can be dropped. Two repeats per configuration are required because the contract grants zero numeric tolerance and a provider that silently returns different numbers for an identical request must be caught rather than assumed stable. Both locales are sent because they are different models that must never be pooled: en-US is the only Azure configuration that names a produced phone, and en-AU is the only Azure configuration calibrated for Australian speech, so omitting either would remove evidence the checkpoint is meant to report. Child clips, held out clips, Australian Common Voice, the timing fixture, the Common Phone set and the LibriSpeech subset are all excluded because none of them is needed to answer this question.
checkpoint_22e4_transmission_plan.owner_decision: Adam approved this volume explicitly in the working session on 2026-07-25 after being shown that it raises the transmitted sample from five clips to the full adult development and tuning set, and that both locales would be sent.

sending any recording of Adam or of any other person
treating any returned score as reference truth or as Australian truth

checkpoint_22e4b_transmission_plan.en_au_note: Checkpoint 22E4 confirmed that en-AU names zero of its phone positions and therefore produced no scorable evidence at all. Sending it the powered sample cannot change that and is expected to reconfirm it. It is sent anyway by explicit owner decision, so the record shows every eligible lane measured on identical evidence.
checkpoint_22e4b_transmission_plan.justification: The frozen selection gates must be evaluated separately on the development and the threshold tuning adult partitions, so both are required and neither can be dropped. Checkpoint 22E4 used a fraction of the adult speakers this project already holds and its outcome turned on 34 positive tuning opportunities and a difference of two flags, so the smallest sample that answers the powered question is every non held out adult. Two repeats per configuration are required because the contract grants zero numeric tolerance. Both locales are sent because they are different models that must never be pooled, and because the owner decided that every eligible lane receives the same powered sample so that no lane can be described as having been reduced after it failed to produce evidence. Child clips, held out clips, Australian Common Voice, the timing fixture, the Common Phone set and the LibriSpeech subset are all excluded because none of them is needed to answer this question.
checkpoint_22e4b_transmission_plan.owner_decision: Adam approved this volume explicitly on 2026-07-27, after being shown the audio hours, the Azure Australia East standard rate of A$1.4492 per audio hour, the resulting cost of about A$14, and the A$289.83 of account credit remaining. He also moved the Speech resource from the free F0 tier to standard S0 himself, because the free tier allows five audio hours a month and would have truncated the run.
